territory: Cross-cutting lens: Next.js App Router caching and revalidation across the whole app — every revalidatePath call site, the mutation→revalidation map, Router Cache semantics (Next 16.3.1 verified against node_modules/next/dist), layout-vs-page render boundaries, per-request work in layouts, proxy.ts allowlist vs route tree, static/dynamic rendering, fetch caching, and streaming/error-boundary behavior

findings.title: drainMailQueue can never select 'deletion-scheduled' rows: the account-deletion confirmation/takeover-alarm email is queued and never sent
findings.expected: requestAccountDeletion queues a 'deletion-scheduled' email (its comment: 'the takeover alarm: if somebody else did this, the mail says how to undo it while the window is still open'), and a later drain pass sends it with priority 20, same class as password-changed.
findings.actual: The ONLY selector that pulls rows out of the queue filters on kind IN eligibleKinds, and eligibleKinds is always either ["verify", "reset", "password-changed"] or ["reset", "password-changed"]. 'deletion-scheduled' appears in neither list, so the row sits status='queued' forever. The member never gets the written confirmation, a victim of an account takeover never gets the alarm during the 60-day window in which sign-in undoes the deletion, and mailHealth/backlog counts the stuck row as 'waiting' permanently.
findings.evidence: src/lib/email-queue.ts:53: `export type MailKind = "verify" | "reset" | "password-changed" | "deletion-scheduled";` — the kind exists, has PRIORITY 20 ('The same class of message as password-changed'), a per-user enqueue cap at line 281, and a render branch at line 394 (`if (row.kind === "deletion-scheduled") {`). But inside drainMailQueue: `const eligibleKinds = live.verifyRemaining > 0 ? ["verify", "reset", "password-changed"] : ["reset", "password-changed"];` followed by `const next = await prisma.outboundEmail.findFirst({ where: { status: "queued", kind: { in: eligibleKinds }, ... } })`. Every send path funnels here: enqueueMail calls scheduleDrain() (line 350) which calls drainMailQueue; the (main) layout's after() calls drainMailQueue; verificationMailState only fast-paths kind='verify' rows. There is no other sender. scripts/qa/phase8-probe.mjs:180-181 only asserts the row was QUEUED, never that it can drain, which is how this passed the audit.
findings.fixDirection: Add "deletion-scheduled" to both branches of eligibleKinds (it is a security notice, so it belongs beside "reset" and "password-changed" in the reserve-only branch too). Then sweep existing stuck rows: any OutboundEmail with kind='deletion-scheduled' and status='queued' will start draining on the next page view once deployed.
findings.gateOrTest: A unit test in src/lib (mjs, alongside gate-coverage.test.mjs) asserting every member of MailKind is selectable by the drain filter — i.e. the union of the two eligibleKinds arrays equals the MailKind set — so the next added kind cannot silently strand either.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (proving it live requires writing a deletion request against the shared production database). The quoted filter vs the type union is decisive on its own.

findings.title: All 12 /admin pages rely solely on the layout gate, which does not run on page-segment RSC requests: demoted admins keep reading admin data during a session, and a crafted router-state request may fetch admin page data with only a member session
findings.expected: Every admin page render re-establishes that the requester is an admin before returning member emails, verification states, login attempts, audit rows, reports and analytics.
findings.actual: requireAdminPage() runs only in admin/layout.tsx. Grep confirms none of the 12 admin page.tsx files (nor their query helpers, e.g. lib/admin-people-query.ts) call auth()/requireAdminPage — they are bare prisma reads. In App Router partial rendering, a navigation request renders only the segments the client's Next-Router-State-Tree marks as changed: node_modules/next/dist/server/app-render/walk-tree-with-flight-router-state.js gates rendering on `renderComponentsOnThisLevel` derived from the client-sent flightRouterState, and the staleTimes doc states 'shared layouts won't automatically be refetched on every navigation, only the page segment that changes'. Two consequences: (1) an admin demoted mid-session who is already inside /admin keeps soft-navigating between admin subpages and receiving fresh admin data — the layout gate never re-runs and the pages never check (role demotion does not bump credentialVersion, and even if it did, no code on these renders reads the session at all); (2) a regular member who crafts an RSC request whose router-state-tree marks the admin layout segment as already-known may receive the page segment's flight data — the proxy only checks that a session cookie EXISTS, and nothing else in the render path checks anything.
findings.evidence: src/app/(main)/admin/layout.tsx: `await requireAdminPage(); const counts = await loadAdminCounts();` is the only gate. src/app/(main)/admin/people/page.tsx: `const [page, total] = await Promise.all([loadPeoplePage(filters), prisma.user.count({ where: peopleWhere(filters) })]);` — no session read. lib/admin.ts's own comment concedes the design: 'A layout guard is navigation, not authorisation' — but applies that reasoning only to server actions, while the PAGES render the same protected data. walk-tree-with-flight-router-state.js:58-119: `const renderComponentsOnThisLevel = ...` / `if (renderComponentsOnThisLevel) {` — the server renders only what the client's header claims is missing.
findings.fixDirection: Call requireAdminPage() at the top of every admin page (or, cheaper, inside the shared data helpers: loadPeoplePage, the audit/reports/analytics/mail/content/messages/support/catchups loaders), exactly as every admin server action already calls requireAdmin(). Keep the layout call for the counts. This is one line per page and removes both the demotion window and the crafted-request question entirely.
findings.gateOrTest: Extend src/lib/gate-coverage.test.mjs to assert every file matching src/app/(main)/admin/**/page.tsx contains a requireAdminPage( call (same pattern the repo already uses to pin deleted routes deleted).
findings.reproPlan: Live, read-only: sign in via /api/dev-login as a NON-admin member on the local dev server, then GET /admin/people with headers `RSC: 1` and a Next-Router-State-Tree copied from a real admin session's request but with the layout segment marked unchanged; if member data comes back, the crafted-request half is proven. The demoted-admin half is provable from the quoted code alone.

findings.title: The notification bell badge is frozen for the entire browsing session: the (main) layout only computes unreadCount on hard loads, and NotificationBell ignores every later value
findings.expected: The bell badge reflects unread notifications with reasonable freshness: it rises when a like/comment/catch-up notification arrives during a session (the component even ships a shake animation for exactly that: 'Shakes the bell when the unread count RISES'), and falls when notifications are read on another device or tab.
findings.actual: Three compounding facts make the badge correct only at the moment of a full page load. (1) unreadCount is computed in the (main) layout, and shared layouts are not re-rendered on soft navigation (staleTimes doc: 'shared layouts won't automatically be refetched on every navigation, only the page segment that changes'), so browsing feed→directory→letters never recomputes it. (2) Even when the layout IS re-rendered server-side (any server action that calls revalidatePath re-renders the full current route), `useState(initialUnreadCount)` only reads the prop at mount — the persistent sidebar/mobile-band bell instance never takes the new value. (3) There is no polling anywhere (grep for setInterval/useSWR across components: none), and handleOpen() fetches the notification list but never recomputes unreadCount from it, so the panel can show unread rows while the badge says nothing, and vice versa. Net: the shake-on-rise effect at line 110 is unreachable dead code (unreadCount only ever decreases after mount), a member browsing for an hour never learns of new notifications, and marking things read on the phone leaves the laptop badge lit until reload. There is no /notifications page — the bell is the only notifications surface, so nothing corrects it. Side inconsistency: pages that mount the header-variant bell (e.g. /feed passes a freshly-queried unreadCount through PageHeader) remount per navigation via (main)/template.tsx, so the header bell and the rail bell can show different counts simultaneously.
findings.evidence: layout.tsx:35: `const [unreadCount, mailState] = await Promise.all([prisma.notification.count({ where: { userId: session.user.id, read: false } }), ...])` — layout-scoped. notification-bell.tsx:98: `const [unreadCount, setUnreadCount] = useState(initialUnreadCount);` — prop read once. Lines 160-177: setUnreadCount is only ever called with decrements (`c - 1`) or 0. handleOpen (134-145) sets notifications/nextCursor/hasMore but never unreadCount.
findings.fixDirection: Have the bell own its count: on mount and on a modest interval (or at least on every dropdown open and on window focus), fetch the unread count via the existing getNotifications action (add a count to its return) and setUnreadCount from the server value. That single change fixes the frozen badge, the cross-device case, the panel/badge disagreement, and resurrects the shake animation. Optionally also sync state from initialUnreadCount when the prop changes (an effect comparing prop to a ref) so action-triggered layout re-renders propagate.
findings.gateOrTest: Playwright: sign in, mark all read via a direct server call, poll the badge geometry/count to assert it clears without a reload; and the inverse (insert a notification row, assert the badge appears within the refresh interval).
findings.reproPlan: Live, own-account-only writes on local dev: open two tabs as the same dev-login user; in tab A open the bell and 'Mark all read'; observe tab B's badge stays lit indefinitely through soft navigations and only clears on hard reload.

findings.title: Root layout reads the theme cookie, making every route dynamic — including the landing page the code explicitly promises stays static
findings.expected: The signed-out landing page '/' (and /privacy, /terms, /guidelines) is statically rendered and served from cache. proxy.ts:140-146 documents this as a deliberate decision: 'Handled here rather than in app/page.tsx so the landing page stays statically rendered for logged-out visitors: calling auth() in the page would opt the whole route into dynamic rendering for everyone.'
findings.actual: The ROOT layout awaits cookies() on every request: layout.tsx:68 `const theme = (await getThemeCookie()) ?? "light";` where theme.ts:23 is `const value = (await cookies()).get(THEME_COOKIE)?.value;`. cookies() in the root layout opts the ENTIRE route tree into dynamic rendering (no PPR/cacheComponents is enabled in next.config.ts), so '/' — the most-shared public URL, hit by every prospective member, link preview and crawler — is a full serverless render per request, as are the three policy pages. The care taken in the proxy to avoid auth() in page.tsx buys nothing. At launch-day traffic this is latency and function-invocation cost on the front door, and it also means the framer-motion-heavy landing renders server-side per hit.
findings.evidence: src/app/layout.tsx:68 and src/lib/theme.ts:22-25 quoted above; next.config.ts contains no ppr/cacheComponents flag; proxy.ts:140-146 carries the contradicted design comment.
findings.fixDirection: Stop reading the cookie in the root layout. Options: move the theme-cookie read into the (main) layout only (signed-out pages are always light per the design system), with next-themes handling the client side; or read the cookie in a client component via document.cookie before hydration (next-themes' standard script approach) so the server render stays cookie-free. Verify with `next build` output showing '○ (Static)' for /, /privacy, /terms, /guidelines.
findings.gateOrTest: A check in scripts/qa (or a build assertion) that the build manifest marks '/' as static, so a future request-API read in a shared layout cannot silently regress it again.
findings.reproPlan: Read-only: run `next build` locally and read the route summary table ('ƒ' vs '○' for /). No DB writes involved (build does not seed).

findings.title: verificationMailState performs a blocking Resend send inside the (main) layout's awaited Promise.all — the exact network call the same file's after() comment forbids in the render path
findings.expected: Page render never waits on the mail provider. The layout's own comment (lines 58-62) states the rule: the drain runs 'Inside after(), unlike the catch-up advance, because this one makes network calls to Resend: it must run AFTER the response has been streamed, or every page in the app would wait on somebody else's welcome email.'
findings.actual: For any signed-in member whose email is unconfirmed, the layout awaits verificationMailState(session.user.id) inside the render-blocking Promise.all (layout.tsx:44-46). When the newest verify row is status='queued' and budget remains, that function calls claimAndSend(row) synchronously: 2 DB writes, a token mint, then `await sendMail(...)` — a live Resend API round trip — before the page can render. The Resend SDK's fetch has no timeout, so a hung provider connection stalls the page toward the function ceiling. This hits exactly the newest members (everyone is unconfirmed on signup day), and while Resend is erroring, EVERY page load for such a member retries the send in-path until the row burns its 4 attempts.
findings.evidence: layout.tsx:44-46: `session.user.emailConfirmed ? Promise.resolve(null) : verificationMailState(session.user.id),` inside `await Promise.all([...])`. email-queue.ts:592-596: 'Budget is available, so nothing may sit queued: send it now.' `if (row.status === "queued") { const outcome = await claimAndSend(row); ... }`. claimAndSend (159-240) performs `await sendMail({ to: row.to, ...built })` plus three prisma writes.
findings.fixDirection: Split the function: the layout should only READ state (row status + budget arithmetic, all DB-local) to choose the banner, and the actual send should be scheduled via the existing scheduleDrain()/after() path (the drain already prioritises reset over verify; add a targeted claimAndSend inside after() if first-page-view immediacy matters). The banner can honestly say 'imminent' for a queued row it just scheduled.
findings.gateOrTest: A unit test asserting verificationMailState never invokes sendMail (mock the module and call with a queued row), or an integration assertion that layout render time for an unconfirmed user is independent of Resend latency.
findings.reproPlan: Live, local, own account: create an unconfirmed dev account with EMAIL_DEV_SEND=1 and a deliberately slow/unreachable Resend stub; time any page load — it inherits the provider latency. (Uses the shared DB only for the account's own rows.)

findings.title: Unvalidated numeric searchParams reach Prisma as NaN: /directory?year=abc (or yearFrom/yearTo) throws during render and blanks the whole app shell
findings.expected: A malformed filter value in the URL degrades to 'no filter' or an empty result, never an error page.
findings.actual: where.ts:28: `filters.year === "faculty" ? "faculty" : filters.year ? Number(filters.year) : null` — Number("abc") is NaN, `typeof NaN === "number"` is true, so line 47 sets `where.batchYear = NaN`; same for yearFrom/yearTo at lines 29-30/49-54 (`gte: NaN`). Prisma rejects NaN for an Int filter with a PrismaClientValidationError thrown during the page render, which propagates to the ONLY error boundary in the app (src/app/error.tsx at the root), replacing the entire shell — sidebar included — with the generic 'Something went wrong' screen. The same unvalidated DirectoryFilters object is also accepted verbatim by the loadDirectoryPage server action (actions.ts:39-63 has no Zod parse on filters), so a tampered POST throws server-side there too. Reachable by any shared/mangled URL; the year comes straight from searchParams (page.tsx:198 mirrors the same Number() parse).
findings.evidence: Quoted lines above; directory/page.tsx:187-216 passes `params.year` etc. into buildDirectoryWhere with no sanitisation; no error.tsx exists between the root and the directory page (find over src/app returned only src/app/error.tsx).
findings.fixDirection: Parse the numeric filters defensively in one place (buildDirectoryWhere): Number.isInteger(n) within a plausible year range (e.g. 1930..current+1) or drop the filter. Apply the same coercion inside loadDirectoryPage (a small Zod schema for DirectoryFilters would satisfy the actions-validate-everything rule).
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test on buildDirectoryWhere with year='abc', yearFrom='-1', yearTo='1e99' asserting no NaN reaches the returned where; plus one verify:shot of /directory?year=abc expecting the normal page.
findings.reproPlan: Live, read-only: signed in on local dev, open /directory?year=abc and observe the error screen; server log shows PrismaClientValidationError.

findings.title: Fire-and-forget telemetry writes (login attempts, search log, token sweep) are not scheduled via after(): on Vercel the instance can freeze before they land
findings.expected: Bookkeeping writes that must not block the response still reliably execute — on serverless that means after()/waitUntil, which this codebase already uses correctly for the mail drain (layout.tsx:63) and scheduleDrain (email-queue.ts:373 with its `after(run)` + fallback).
findings.actual: Five write paths use bare `void promise` instead: login-attempt.ts:46 `void prisma.loginAttempt.create(...)` (called from authorize() — the data feeding the admin 'who cannot sign in' panel the file's own comment calls the one place the owner would notice a locked-out member); search-log.ts is `void logSearch(...)`-ed from users/search:72, places/search:127 and the feed page render at feed/page.tsx:31; auth-tokens.ts:107 `void prisma.authToken.deleteMany(...)` (the only sweep keeping the token table bounded — 'a project that has no cron'). On Vercel, execution freezes when the response finishes; work merely detached with void has no guarantee of completing, so these rows are dropped intermittently — worst exactly under burst/cold-start conditions, which is when login-failure analytics matter most, and the token sweep silently never running lets AuthToken grow unbounded.
findings.evidence: login-attempt.ts:44-59: 'Deliberately not awaited... A statistics row must never be able to delay, or fail, a sign-in' — the intent is right, the mechanism is wrong for serverless. Contrast email-queue.ts:364-373 which does `try { after(run); } catch { void run(); }` — the codebase already owns the correct pattern.
findings.fixDirection: Wrap each in the same after()-with-void-fallback helper scheduleDrain uses (extract it to a shared lib). recordLoginAttempt runs inside NextAuth's authorize where after() is available in Next 16 (server function context); keep the void fallback for contexts without a request scope.
findings.gateOrTest: Grep-based gate in the unit tests: no `void prisma.` outside an after() wrapper in src/lib and src/app (the repo already runs source-grep tests in security-regressions.test.mjs).
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only: platform freeze behavior cannot be reproduced meaningfully on a local long-lived dev server; the argument rests on Vercel's documented freeze-after-response semantics plus the quoted code.

findings.title: Visit/page-view analytics undercount structurally: touchLastSeen fires only on layout renders, so soft navigations are never counted and lastPath is wrong
findings.expected: The Visit row records page views and the path the member is on: proxy.ts mints x-visit-id 'to attribute page views to one Visit row', last-seen.ts documents 'Visit is NOT throttled: it counts views and follows the path, which is the whole point', and the layout comment claims it runs on 'essentially every authenticated page view'.
findings.actual: touchLastSeen is awaited only in the (main) LAYOUT (layout.tsx:51), and shared layouts do not re-render on soft navigation (Next 16 staleTimes doc: 'shared layouts won't automatically be refetched on every navigation, only the page segment that changes'). An SPA session of 30 page views registers as views:1 (the initial hard load) plus one view per server-action-triggered refresh; Visit.lastPath and the x-pathname the admin room displays stay pinned to the entry page; entry/exit analysis, average-views-per-visit and the per-page popularity numbers in /admin/analytics are all systematically wrong — biased toward hard-loading and mutating users. The same limitation quietly reduces advanceDueCatchups and the after() mail-drain tick to hard-loads only (both have cron backstops per audits M27/M34, so for them it is only reduced frequency, not loss).
findings.evidence: layout.tsx:48-51: 'Records that this member was here... Rides in this same Promise.all' — the only call site of touchLastSeen (grep confirms). last-seen.ts:117-162 does the views:{increment:1} upsert. The staleTimes doc quote pins the render semantics.
findings.fixDirection: Count views where every navigation actually passes: either in proxy.ts (it already sees every request and owns the visit cookie — filter to document/RSC page requests via the RSC/next-router-prefetch headers and call a lightweight endpoint or move the upsert behind after() in a route the proxy pings), or client-side: a tiny component in the (main) layout that reports usePathname changes to a server action which does the Visit upsert. The client reporter is the smaller change and also fixes lastPath.
findings.gateOrTest: e2e assertion: sign in, soft-navigate across 4 routes, read the Visit row (views >= 4, lastPath = final route).
findings.reproPlan: Live, own-account: on local dev, sign in, soft-navigate 5 pages, then query the Visit row (read-only inspection via prisma studio is pre-approved) — views will be 1.

findings.title: Server-rendered display dates show the UTC calendar day to IST members: letters, collection photos and admin lists date content written 00:00-05:29 IST on the previous day
findings.expected: A letter published at 1:10 AM IST on the 15th reads '15 August' everywhere; the deletion email names the purge date as the member's calendar experiences it. The codebase knows the rule — wordle.ts:20 uses timeZone:'Asia/Kolkata' ('the valley's day is an IST day') and admin/mail/page.tsx:94 passes timeZone:'Asia/Kolkata' explicitly.
findings.actual: formatDisplayDate (utils.ts:151-157: `new Date(date).toLocaleDateString("en-GB", { day, month, year })` — no timeZone) runs in SERVER components on Vercel (UTC): letters index (letters/page.tsx:163), letter reading page (letters/[id]/page.tsx:165 inline and :188 via formatDisplayDate), collection photo page (collection/[id]/page.tsx:145 inline), admin support and admin catchups lists. Anything created between 00:00 and 05:29 IST — about 23% of the IST day, and precisely the late-night letter-writing hours — renders with the previous day's date, permanently. Same class: settings/actions.ts:344 formats purgeDate with toLocaleDateString('en-GB') and no timeZone, so the deletion email can name a purge date one day early. Secondary: formatTimeAgo's >4-weeks fallback (utils.ts:21) renders in UTC during SSR of client components and re-renders in browser IST after hydration — a hydration mismatch/date flip on old timestamps.
findings.evidence: Quoted call sites; server pages carry no 'use client'; Vercel functions run UTC; members are IST (+5:30) per the brief.
findings.fixDirection: Give formatDisplayDate (and the two inline toLocaleDateString calls in letters/[id] and collection/[id], plus purgeDate in settings/actions.ts) an explicit timeZone: 'Asia/Kolkata', the same decision wordle.ts already made and documented. For formatTimeAgo's fallback, the same fix also removes the hydration mismatch.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test: formatDisplayDate(new Date('2026-08-14T19:00:00Z')) === '15 Aug 2026' (19:00 UTC = 00:30 IST next day).
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only in production terms; locally provable with TZ=UTC node -e using the quoted helper.

findings.title: Clicking a notification whose row was pruned or deleted does nothing: markNotificationRead throws P2025 and the navigation never runs
findings.expected: Tapping a notification always navigates to its link; a missing row is treated as already-read.
findings.actual: actions.ts:77-80: `await prisma.notification.update({ where: { id: notificationId, userId: session.user.id }, data: { read: true } })` — Prisma update throws P2025 when no row matches, and nothing catches it, so the server action rejects. In the client, handleClickNotification (bell.tsx:160-171) does `await markNotificationRead(notif.id);` BEFORE `router.push(notif.link)`; the rejection aborts the handler, so the tap is silently dead. Reachable whenever the panel holds rows the DB no longer has: the KEEP=100 prune (actions.ts:44-57) runs on every first-page open in any OTHER tab/device, and getNotifications caps a session at 100 visible rows across two surfaces (header bell + rail bell keep independent lists), so a stale second panel is a normal state, not an exotic one. Also note both mark actions call revalidatePath("/") (actions.ts:82,95) — the landing page, not any surface that renders notifications; under Next 16 semantics its only real effect is forcing a full re-render of whatever page the member is on for every single notification click.
findings.evidence: Quoted lines; no try/catch around the update; the client handler's await precedes router.push.
findings.fixDirection: Use updateMany (returns count 0 instead of throwing) or catch P2025 and return success; in the client, run router.push regardless of the mark call's outcome. Drop the revalidatePath("/") calls (the client already updates optimistically, and the like-button work in feed/actions.ts:514 documents why the forced refresh is unwanted).
findings.gateOrTest: Unit-level: markNotificationRead with a nonexistent id returns { success: true } rather than throwing.
findings.reproPlan: Live, own-account, local dev: open the bell in two tabs with >100 notifications, open tab A (prunes), then in tab B click a pruned row — nothing happens; console shows the rejected action.

findings.title: setTheme's cookie write triggers the exact full-page action refresh the like-button work removed: toggling theme mid-scroll re-renders the whole route and can scroll-jump
findings.expected: Theme toggling is client-side and cosmetic: the action's own comment says 'Deliberately revalidates nothing: theme is cosmetic... the client flips the class instantly via next-themes' own setTheme.'
findings.actual: Setting a cookie in a server action marks the request as revalidated regardless of any revalidatePath call: node_modules/next/dist/server/web/spec-extension/adapters/request-cookies.js:130 sets `workStore.pathWasRevalidated = ActionDidRevalidateStaticAndDynamic` on any mutable-cookie write, and action-handler.js then re-renders the full current route in the action response (skipPageRendering false) and instructs the client to drop its router cache (NEXT_ACTION_REVALIDATED_HEADER). So every theme toggle server-re-renders the current page (layout queries included) and applies a fresh tree — the same mechanism feed/actions.ts:514-517 documents as 'landing as an occasional scroll-to-top on the heart click (root cause of the heart scroll-jump bug)'. A member toggling dark mode mid-feed pays a full server render and risks the same jump; the comment's premise ('revalidates nothing') is false.
findings.evidence: theme-actions.ts:33: `(await cookies()).set(THEME_COOKIE, theme, {...})` inside the action; request-cookies.js:130 and action-handler.js:100-131/990 quoted mechanics.
findings.fixDirection: Set the cookie client-side (it is deliberately httpOnly:false and holds only 'light'/'dark') via document.cookie in the same client handler that calls next-themes setTheme, and let the server action persist only User.theme. That removes the cookie write from the action and with it the forced refresh.
findings.gateOrTest: chrome-devtools check pinned by a Playwright spec: toggle theme at scrollY>0 on /feed, expect.poll scrollY unchanged and no full RSC page payload in the action response.
findings.reproPlan: Live, read-only-ish (writes only the member's own theme): on local dev, scroll the feed, toggle theme, watch the network tab — the action response carries the full flight tree, and scroll position occasionally resets.

findings.title: One error boundary for the whole app: any single page's render error replaces the entire shell, and most degradation paths funnel to a full-screen generic error
findings.expected: A render error in one page's data (a Prisma hiccup on /letters, the NaN case above, a bad row) degrades to an in-shell error state: the sidebar, navigation and the rest of the app stay usable.
findings.actual: find over src/app shows exactly one error boundary, src/app/error.tsx at the root (there is also no global-error.tsx, so an error IN the root layout itself — e.g. the theme cookie read or a DB failure in the (main) layout's awaited Promise.all, which contains the un-suppressed `prisma.notification.count` — falls back to Next's default error page rather than the branded one). Because every page streams under a loading.tsx with status 200 first, a mid-render throw swaps the ENTIRE tree — chrome included — for the bare 'Something went wrong' screen with no navigation, and 'Try again' re-renders from the root. For the 2,000-user launch, one flaky query on one route momentarily presents as the whole site being down to that member.
findings.evidence: find output listed in the transcript: only src/app/error.tsx and src/app/not-found.tsx exist besides loading files; (main)/layout.tsx:35-41 awaits prisma.notification.count with no catch (unlike its advanceDueCatchups/touchLastSeen neighbours which swallow internally).
findings.fixDirection: Add an error.tsx inside (main)/ (renders within AppShell, keeping the sidebar) and optionally per heavy section (feed, letters, catchups, admin); add a global-error.tsx so a root-layout failure still shows branded copy. Consider try/catching the unreadCount query to 0 in the layout, matching the stated contract of its sibling calls.
findings.gateOrTest: A gate-coverage-style test asserting (main)/error.tsx exists; manual verify:shot of a page throwing behind the (main) boundary showing the sidebar intact.
findings.reproPlan: Live, read-only: /directory?year=abc (finding above) currently demonstrates the full-shell blank-out on local dev.

verifiedClean: 6c 'use cache'/unstable_cache/react cache() capturing per-user data in shared scope: NONE in app code — the only cache() is React's request-scoped cache around auth() (src/lib/auth.ts:396), which is correct dedupe, not cross-request; no unstable_cache or 'use cache' anywhere in src/

6c fetch() caching in data paths: the single cached fetch is src/lib/wordle.ts:36 (next:{revalidate:3600}) — shared, non-user data, URL keyed per IST day; all other fetches are client-side or third-party POSTs (razorpay, turnstile) with default no-store — CLEAN

6c static rendering vs cookies / generateStaticParams: no generateStaticParams anywhere; no page reads DB at build time (landing and policies are content-only); the catchups/join/[token] public page calls auth() so it can never be ISR-cached with stale invite state — CLEAN (aside from the root-layout-dynamic finding)

6c revalidatePath mistargets are inert under Next 16.3.1 semantics: verified in node_modules/next/dist (action-handler.js skipPageRendering, revalidate.js pathWasRevalidated) that ANY revalidatePath in an action re-renders the full current route and purges the client router cache regardless of path match, and every (main) route is dynamic with staleTimes.dynamic=0 — so '/admin' vs '/admin/messages/[id]', dead '/groups/*' paths (proxy redirects all /groups to /catchups), and admin-actions' path forms cause no member-visible staleness; the mutation→surface map (posts→/feed+/letters+/profile, collection→/collection(+/[id]) , messages→threads, catchups→its 3 surfaces, settings/profile→/settings+/profile) is covered on next visit by dynamic rendering

6c router-cache staleness after mutations: staleTimes.dynamic default 0 confirmed in the bundled docs — soft navigations always refetch page segments, so only back/forward reuse serves stale payloads, which is Next's deliberate design — CLEAN

6c proxy.ts publicPaths vs route tree: walked all 90 routes against the allowlist — no NEW reachable-but-unintended route (dev-login 404s in production builds, catchups/join is token-regex-scoped and thin by design, /hoopoe is a no-data client page, crons self-authenticate via CRON_SECRET, /api/demo/reset guarded by IS_DEMO+force-dynamic, demo closed-path lists mirror the route set); no admin API route relies on proxy cookie-presence alone (all four checked handlers self-auth)

6i layout-blast-radius concurrency on the lazy catch-up advance: advanceEdition uses a compare-and-swap (applyEditionAction returns false on lost CAS, caller re-reads) and openNextRoundIfDue CASes nextOpensAt→null inside a transaction with the [catchupId,number] unique as backstop — concurrent page loads cannot double-advance — CLEAN

6i mail-drain concurrency from many simultaneous layouts: claimAndSend claims via conditional updateMany on status='queued' (count 0 → lost-claim), stale claims reclaimed after 2 min, dev/demo processes hard-refuse via queueIsSendable — CLEAN (except the eligibleKinds finding)

6j API list endpoints bounded: users/search take:8 + rate-limited + verified-email gated; users-by-batch take:5000 (fine at 2,000 users); notifications keyset-paginated take≤50 with self-pruning table; directory keyset take:61 with id tiebreak in every orderBy — CLEAN
6b sequential awaits in the two heaviest pages: feed/page.tsx and profile/[id]/page.tsx batch their queries with Promise.all — CLEAN

Route handler response caching: Next 16 route handlers are dynamic by default, /api/account/export explicitly no-store, no handler sets a public Cache-Control — no per-user API response can be shared — CLEAN

(main) layout redirect vs page auth for MEMBER pages: every (main) page that renders member data calls auth() itself (only /about, /birds, /donate skip it, and they render no per-user or private data) — the layout-gate weakness is confined to the /admin cluster reported above
